title: Regional token COGS playbook and optimization scenarios
body:
Purpose:
A compact, reproducible spreadsheet-style snapshot for per-region hosted API token COGS and recommended levers. This is a lab playbook: quick scenarios (Baseline / Caching / Quant+Batch) to approximate per-1k-token COGS and margin impact across three representative regions. Use for planning pricing/regional routing experiments and to drive prioritized infra/product work.

Top-line assumptions (global):
- Time window: monthly steady-state workloads (30 days)
- Representative request mix: 60% short completions (avg 80 tokens), 30% medium (avg 400 tokens), 10% long (avg 2,000 tokens)
- Tokenization ratio: 1.02 (whitespace model)
- Customer list price per 1k tokens (example): US = $0.80, EU = $0.95, AP = $1.05 (reflects regional price adjustments).

Cost building blocks (per-region):
- GPU hourly + amortized infra: region-specific (see table)
- Networking egress: per-GB varying by region (included in micro COGS)
- Worker utilization: baseline 55% (no batching/caching), mid 70% (caching), optimized 85% (quant+batch)
- KV/prefix cache hit: baseline 5%, caching scenario 22%, optimized 35%
- Model variants: full-fp32 equivalent vs int8 quant variant (weight reduction). Quant variant reduces GPU latency and increases throughput (modeled as 1.5x effective throughput on same HW).

Quick region cost table (inputs):
Region | GPU $/hr (amort + infra) | egress $/GB | median seq len | baseline util | local ops overhead %
US (us-east) | 3.50 | 0.09 | 512 | 55% | 12%
EU (eu-west) | 4.10 | 0.11 | 480 | 50% | 14%
AP (ap-southeast) | 5.20 | 0.14 | 420 | 45% | 16%

Workload conversion to GPU-seconds per 1k tokens (simplified parametric model):
- baseline: 1k tokens -> 0.28 GPU-sec (long-tail dependent)
- caching: reduces repeated prefix compute -> 0.22 GPU-sec
- quant+batch: improves per-token throughput -> 0.18 GPU-sec
(These come from runtime bench microtests; treat as knobs to sweep)

Derived micro-COGS per 1k tokens (compute only):
Region | Baseline compute $/1k | Caching compute $/1k | Quant+Batch compute $/1k
US | $0.00027 * (3.50/1hr) scaled -> computed below | ... | ...
(Explicit numbers below from applied calculation)

Explicit scenario numbers (computed):
- US (us-east): GPU $/hr = $3.50 => $/sec = $0.0009722
  - Baseline compute: 0.28s * $0.0009722 = $0.0002722 per 1k tokens
  - Caching compute: 0.22s * $0.0009722 = $0.0002139 per 1k tokens
  - Quant+Batch compute: 0.18s * $0.0009722 = $0.00017499 per 1k tokens
  - Add egress and overhead (approx): baseline + $0.012 (egress + infra ops) -> baseline total COGS ≈ $0.01227/1k
  - Caching total COGS ≈ $0.01222/1k (small improvement on egress effect)
  - Quant+Batch total COGS ≈ $0.01190/1k

- EU (eu-west): GPU $/hr = $4.10 => $/sec = $0.0011389
  - Baseline compute: 0.28s * $0.0011389 = $0.0003189 per 1k tokens
  - Caching: 0.22s -> $0.0002506
  - Quant+Batch: 0.18s -> $0.0002050
  - Add egress + overhead baseline $0.0135 -> totals: baseline $0.01382, caching $0.01375, quant+batch $0.01371

- AP (ap-southeast): GPU $/hr = $5.20 => $/sec = $0.0014444
  - Baseline compute: 0.28s * $0.0014444 = $0.0004044 per 1k tokens
  - Caching: 0.22s -> $0.0003178
  - Quant+Batch: 0.18s -> $0.0002600
  - Add egress + overhead baseline $0.015 -> totals: baseline $0.01540, caching $0.01532, quant+batch $0.01526

Per-1k-token margin snapshots (using example price per 1k):
Customer price (per 1k) | Region baseline COGS | Baseline margin | Quant+Batch margin
US $0.80 | COGS $0.01227 -> margin ≈ $0.7877 (98.5%) | optimized COGS $0.01190 -> margin ≈ $0.7881
EU $0.95 | COGS $0.01382 -> margin ≈ $0.9362 | optimized COGS $0.01371 -> margin ≈ $0.9363
AP $1.05 | COGS $0.01540 -> margin ≈ $1.0346 | optimized COGS $0.01526 -> margin ≈ $1.0347

Notes: margins look large because our per-1k token hosted price example is high relative to micro-COGS: compute per token is tiny. The important numbers are relative improvements and absolute delta per million tokens.

Delta per 1M tokens (impact scale):
- US baseline -> quant+batch: savings = ($0.01227 - $0.01190) * 1000 = $0.37 per million tokens? (recompute properly)
  Correct calculation: savings per 1k = $0.01227 - $0.01190 = $0.00037. For 1M tokens (1,000 * 1k units) => $0.37 per 1M tokens.
- EU savings per 1M = ($0.01382 - $0.01371)*1000 = $0.11
- AP savings per 1M = ($0.01540 - $0.01526)*1000 = $0.14
Observation: micro-COGS delta is small in absolute dollars; ops and pricing levers matter more at scale (dedicated pricing, reserved capacity, and batching policies).

Breakdown sensitivity rows (quick):
- If baseline utilization increases from 55% -> 70% (better packing/routeing) compute cost drops ~21% on compute contribution. For US baseline compute $0.0002722 -> becomes $0.000215 (approx). Big lever.
- If cache hit rises to 35% from 5% for short/medium mixes, the effective GPU-seconds per 1k drops from 0.28 -> 0.20 (~29% improvement). Larger than quant alone.
- Quantization combined with 2x effective throughput gives ~30-40% compute improvement on heavy models.

Priority action list (ranked: impact / effort):
1) Short-term (low effort, high impact):
   - Route short-chat-heavy customers to region-level prefix cache edge (trial in us-east). Estimated implementation: 2 sprints infra + 1 product flag. Expected delta: +15–25% effective reduction in tokens hitting long compute.
   - Small product change: enable per-route batching (windowed 10–20ms) for non-interactive endpoints. Impact: utilization +10–15%.
2) Mid-term (medium effort):
   - Introduce quant variants for heavy-usage model families (A/B test one family in eu-west). Effort: model onboarding + runtime kernel path changes (4–6 sprints). Impact: 20–50% throughput improvement on those families.
   - Regional reserved capacity pilots for AP and EU to lower GPU $/hr. Contract negotiation + capacity planning.
3) Long-term (higher effort, high impact):
   - Advanced routing tier: cost-aware routing by model/regional COGS + latency SLO. Benefit: shift non-SLA-sensitive traffic to cheaper regions and to quant variants automatically.
   - Persistent KV prefix cache globally with eviction policies tuned by route.

Quick ROI back-of-envelope for caching pilot (us-east):
- Suppose short requests are 60% of traffic. If cache hit moves from 5% -> 30% for these, overall effective GPU-seconds drop ~20%. On a 1B token/mo tenant, savings = 1B/1k * $0.0002722 * 0.20 ≈ $54,440/mo. Implementation cost estimate: ~$80k infra + 2 engineers 2 months => payback ~1.5–3 months depending on adoption.

Implementation checklist (starter):
- [ ] Define per-route cache eligibility rules (product)
- [ ] Instrument token-level tracing for cache hit/miss attribution (SRE)
- [ ] Small canary: route 5% of short-chat to cached path (us-east)
- [ ] Run 30-day telemetry and compute measured delta vs model (validate bench assumptions)
- [ ] If positive, scale to EU pilot then AP; communicate pricing impacts to GTM for reserved capacity offers

Open questions / TODOs:
- We need a more granular model of egress per token (current model lumps it). Request network micro-bench to quantify tokens->MB mapping for common request mixes.
- Confirm GPU $/hr blended numbers including OS/infra + amortization of reserved instances for Dedicated customers (some costs are cross-subsidized).
- Estimate engineering effort more precisely for quant rollout (kernel path acceptance tests + poison-case validation).

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally conservative with compute time numbers; full optimization will require bench matrix across guest sequence lengths and request mixes.
- The playbook is designed for quick prioritization: caching + batching + utilization improvements yield the largest immediate delta; quantization and reserved capacity compound gains.

Maya Chen — product-optimize
